tagline: The river towns give way to the delta.
intro: From the farming country around Tallulah, the drive works down through Louisiana's river towns toward Venice at the southern tip of the Mississippi Delta. Tallulah grew on cotton worked by enslaved African Americans. In the 1920s its airfield sent up planes to dust the fields against the boll weevil, and Delta Air Lines grew out of that outfit, Delta Dusters.

Farther down, Port Allen's riverfront looks across the Mississippi toward Baton Rouge. At the far end the work changes to commercial fishing and offshore oil and gas service, with anglers leaving Venice for Port Eads near the river's mouth.

moments.title: Waterproof
moments.text: The village took its name from its relative safety from floods before the Mississippi levee system was built.

moments.title: Donaldsonville
moments.text: On the Mississippi's west bank, the town elected attorney and Methodist minister Pierre Caliste Landry mayor in 1868, the first African American elected mayor in the United States.

moments.title: Venice
moments.text: Highway 23 reaches the last community along the Mississippi that a car can reach, the southern end of the Great River Road, nicknamed the end of the world.
